ns2:course.label: Economics of Food and Environmental Justice
ns2:course.description: Access to food and a healthy environment varies across rural/urban location, race, gender, and income in the U.S. Students in this course will analyze questions of "food justice" and "environmental justice" through the lens of economic theory. Students will learn important concepts in the scholarship of minority cultures, learn facts about how food security and experience of environmental quality varies among groups in the U.S., and learn how to use economic theory to understand those patterns and analyze policies to correct inequities. Prerequisite: ACE 100 or ECON 102 or consent of instructor.
ns2:course.courseSectionInformation: Prerequisite: ACE 100 or ECON 102 or consent of instructor.
